lines.vo: Your mind is somewhere else almost half of your waking day.
That's not laziness. That's your brain's default setting.
So Tasha parks her loose thoughts in her Life Reset Planner.
Harvard researchers pinged about two thousand two hundred fifty adults at random moments of their day.
lines.cap: Harvard researchers pinged about 2,250 adults at random moments of their day.

lines.vo: Their minds were wandering roughly forty seven percent of the time.
lines.cap: Their minds were wandering roughly 47% of the time.

lines.vo: And on average, people felt less happy while their minds wandered than while they were focused.
Getting loose thoughts out of your head and onto a page can make it easier to come back.
Notice it, write it, come back. That's how you stay on track.

hook: Your mind is *elsewhere* half the day
